newsitem.title: ESTONIA: MARKET CAUTIOUS OVER TALLINNA LATVIA MOVE.
newsitem.headline: MARKET CAUTIOUS OVER TALLINNA LATVIA MOVE.

text.p: Dealers were cautious in their reactions to news on Thursday that Estonia's Tallinna Pank has in principle agreed to take over Latvian Saules bank.
"It is hard to say, local investors will see it as positive, but the fundmantals of the company suggest that the market's reaction will be negative," one trader said.
"We still need more time to consider what this means for the company," another dealer said.
The bank was higher by the close of trade at 63.10 kroons versus 62.45 kroons although trade was a low 965,136 kroons.
Tallinna Pank earlier told a news conference that it had in principle agreed to increase its stake to 100 percent in the Latvian Saules Banka.
"There is a cat and mouse game with it at the moment as the price tries to find a clear direction," a trader said.
However, dealers would like to see how the bank can keep its market share in Tallinn as well as merge with the Latvian bank.
"I would like to see how much this will cost the bank and what is there strategy for the move," another trader said.
Analysts were also waiting on more information on both how to finance the deal on Saules Banks.
"I think that the deal depends on the pricing schedule. It will most likey be by a share swap which is less costly for the company," Katrin Kaarli, analyst with Hansapank, told Reuters.
